what: caption.py's default --min-duration lengthened a short last cue past the end of the input's picture: on a 3.13 s VFR clip a 0.4 s cue at 2.8 s became 2.8-3.8 s, so --mode mux wrote a 3.8 s container around the 3.13 s picture (.mkv and .mp4; a copy export keeps it) and a burn's adjusted SRT and generated ASS named times no frame has. A cue whose own end was past the picture (an auto-timed --text line, a transcript timed for a longer cut) ran on the same way. The result said only `extended`, and verified: true.
escaped: layout_cues capped the lengthening at the next cue's start and had no bound for the last cue: it was given no picture end, though caption.py had probed the input. The tests of --min-duration used cues well inside the clip, and a burn hides the overrun (its picture is the clip's, 3.146 s before and after), so only a mux's container length or the sidecar's last time shows it; tests/sweep.py's caption row uses --text cues inside the clip and compares the result, not the length.
mechanism: caption.layout_cues takes picture_end (the video stream's own end on the file's clock, emit.own_end less emit.file_origin, given by lay_out, the one step every cue source goes through in burn and mux): a cue that starts before it and would end after it, lengthened or as asked, ends there and is named in a note; one that starts at or after it is not lengthened. tests/test_picture.py's test_a_cue_ends_with_the_picture_it_is_laid_on runs a generated VFR clip through mux .mkv, mux .mp4 and burn, with the cue's end carried past the picture by --min-duration and by its own time, and checks the delivered length, the sidecar's time and the note, and that a cue wholly after the picture is not lengthened. docs/design-decisions.md states the rule beside cues_outside.
